title: Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease
summary: Depression in older adults may be more than a mental health concern. Scientists discovered that accumulating tau protein, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, was linked to worsening depressive symptoms in people who still had normal memory and thinking abilities. The faster tau built up in the brain, the faster depressive symptoms increased, suggesting that mood changes could emerge before cognitive decline.

title: Ancient rocks from the Moon’s far side rewrite the Solar System’s violent past
summary: Scientists studying ancient rocks from the Moon’s far side have uncovered surprising evidence that challenges decades of thinking about the Solar System’s violent past. Instead of a single catastrophic bombardment, asteroid impacts appear to have declined gradually over billions of years, revealing new clues about Earth's early evolution and the origins of life.

title: Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
summary: Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.

title: A black hole the size of an atom could destroy an entire star
summary: MIT scientists have discovered that tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang could slowly devour stars from within, eventually triggering spectacular explosions visible across galaxies. Detecting these unusual cosmic events could reveal the existence of primordial black holes and help solve the mystery of dark matter.

title: Earth’s ancient oceans may have fooled scientists about its oxygen history
summary: Earth’s journey from an oxygen-starved world to a planet capable of supporting complex life may have unfolded very differently than scientists once believed. A new analysis suggests that oxygen accumulated in the atmosphere in three major stages, with the oceans taking millions or even hundreds of millions of years to catch up.

title: New nose drops restore youthful memory and fight Alzheimer’s in aging mice
summary: A revolutionary new nasal treatment has restored youthful learning and memory performance in aging mice while preventing severe cognitive decline in mice with Alzheimer’s-like disease. Developed using technology similar to COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, the nose drops stimulate production of a brain-protecting protein that strengthens neurons and supports memory. Remarkably, the treatment preserved brain function without removing Alzheimer’s-associated plaques, suggesting a completely different way to combat cognitive decline.

title: America is building just 10% of the power lines it needs, experts warn
summary: America’s power grid is falling dangerously behind as electricity demand skyrockets, fueled by data centers, electric vehicles, and industry. The U.S. is building only 10% of the new high-voltage transmission lines experts say it needs, threatening higher energy prices and greater blackout risks. Researchers argue that political obstacles and outdated regulations, rather than technological limitations, are the real problem.

title: A simple metal is hiding a strange new form of magnetism
summary: Scientists have discovered a strange form of magnetism in an ordinary-looking metal that has no overall magnetization yet profoundly changes how electrons behave. The breakthrough offers a promising new path toward understanding exotic quantum materials and developing future electronic technologies.

title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age
summary: A major analysis of 149 studies found that cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non-users, with the difference growing to more than six years among adults 30 and older. Researchers warn that cannabis-related psychiatric risks may accumulate over time, challenging the belief that using marijuana after adolescence is relatively safe.

title: Earth's next ice age may have already begun. Global warming stopped it
summary: Scientists have uncovered surprising evidence that Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be stopped by global warming. By studying ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers discovered that the remnants of a massive ice sheet began expanding again about 2,000 years ago, signaling the possible start of a new glacial period. But by the 1960s, rising temperatures had reversed that growth, causing the ice to shrink instead.

title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat
summary: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, potentially explaining why some people struggle to find relief.

title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.

title: 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck reveals an ingenious waterproofing trick
summary: A 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck has revealed sophisticated waterproofing techniques involving pine tar and beeswax. Microscopic pollen grains trapped in the ancient coatings are now helping scientists reconstruct where the vessel may have traveled and undergone repairs more than two millennia ago.
